question: A signup form 'looks fine' in Figma but fails keyboard and screen-reader use. What concrete checks do you run before handoff?
shortAnswer: Verify labels, focus order, error announcements, contrast, and visible focus states—not only visual layout.
strongAnswer: Ensure every input has a persistent label (not placeholder-only), logical tab order, descriptive error text tied to fields, sufficient color contrast, and non-color-only cues. Spec focus states and hit target sizes. Call out ARIA only when native semantics are insufficient. Partner with eng on semantic HTML first.
followUps: How do you test with a screen reader basics?
commonWrongAnswer: Accessibility is an engineering-only concern after pixels are done.
productionRelevance: Accessible forms reduce support burden and exclusion—often neglected in rush shipping.
